quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus on the road. Any extra task takes attention away from driving and creates danger.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no one is in your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to drive in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can drive only in that direction. The red light means you cannot go any other way. Only proceed if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your mirrors to check for cars passing you. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: What documents must you show when stopped by police?
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your car at all times. You must show all three if stopped by police.

questions.question: What should you check before changing lanes?

options.text: Look over your shoulder for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Then look over your shoulder to spot any vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the others?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions override all signs, signals, and road markings.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down and let the blind pedestrian cross. Be ready to stop to protect them.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who looks away from the road or daydreams.
A driver who looks at a passenger while talking.
A driver who only watches the car ahead.

questions.explanation: Stay focused on the road. Do not look at passengers, search your car, read, sightsee, or daydream. Keep checking the road, mirrors, and dashboard.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning sign.

questions.question: The amount of space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic
Whether there is a stop sign
Whether you use your turn signals

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Fatigue impairs your driving the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you like a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours impairs you like a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time and coordination. It also harms your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: When you approach railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers
Try to drive around a lowered gate
Ignore how many tracks there are

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the rails.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads
Keep your tires at the right air pressure

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Every person in the car every time you drive

questions.correctAnswerText: Every person in the car every time you drive
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object and hurt others in a crash.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: An orange reflective triangle on the back of a vehicle means:
questions.explanation: An orange reflective triangle means the vehicle travels slower than 25 mph. You see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction they must drive on a one-way street. Drivers must follow the direction shown on the sign.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make it harder to turn, increase your stopping distance, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slowly take your foot off the accelerator. Apply the brakes gently when you are moving very slowly. Then pull off the road to a safe area.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: This is a triangular Yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first. Only stop if necessary.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Edge your car into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Change lanes as little as possible. Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right at intersections with this sign.

questions.question: How can you make sure your physical condition does not affect your safe driving?

options.text: Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.
Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limitations and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slick roads?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, take turns and curves more slowly than normal. Driving too fast on curves in wet or icy conditions is especially dangerous.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other drivers are doing, even if the guard tells you otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. You must stop:

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered crossing gate, a stop sign, a person signaling you to stop, or a train that is close enough to be dangerous. If you are not sure if a train is close enough to cross safely, stop. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, let pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to prevent death or injury while driving.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires filled to the correct pressure.
Slow down when driving in rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth and correct air pressure. Slow down when it is raining. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means you cannot do that action. In this case, the symbol shows a right turn, so right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can affect your driving, including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some prescription or over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, take out the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is to:
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot over your shoulder every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
All passengers must use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under must sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front with an airbag.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working when you drive.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, cross multiple lanes suddenly, or cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows laws you must obey. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about dangers or special situations ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you should change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you when the weather is bad.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of cars behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, you should:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them. Do not make eye contact or hand gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to get away.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as usual.
Can drive faster because they are more alert.
Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: If you are worried, upset, crying, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Emotions distract you because your mind is not on driving. Calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow how quickly you react to hazards on the road. Distracted driving is never safe.
